parsed.why: Patterned recent lethal violence against trans women, hostile religious-court framing, failed implementation and a ward-placement death; no state persecution but weak recourse and media censorship make outing dangerous.

No trans criminalisation and no state-sponsored harassment, but occasional police 'modesty' charges against gender-nonconforming presentation, common individual harassment, no recognition or anti-discrimination machinery, military-rule backdrop.

National document/visa regime, refused or stranded trans travellers, foreign advisories, multi-state facility bans with a documented arrest, custody abuse and official threat-framing, partly offset by courts, hate-crime law and no identity offence.

Decriminalised with a 2024 hate-crime statute expressly covering gender identity and constitutional protections; no documented hostility or visitor-facing restriction, though enforcement and social acceptance are unmeasured.

Decriminalisation is a reading-down leaving sections on the books, no gender-identity protection or anti-discrimination law, documented dismissive policing and violence against gender-nonconforming people, plus hostility aimed at LGBT visitors.
